title: 2 Stars, Functioning App, Not Age Appropriate
body: The App Store categorizes Monkey as being appropriate for anyone above the age of 12; content that is intended to have “Infrequent/Mild Sexual Content and Nudity” and “Infrequent/Mild Profanity or Crude Humor.” From my experience, Monkey, through all its efforts to establish a positive and safe platform, is a host for content fueled with high levels of sexual themes, profanity, crude humor and drug use which can influence young audiences, especially without parent moderation. People wanting to use Monkey only need a valid cell phone to do so. According to Melanie Curtin (2017), the average age for a child to obtain a smart phone is 10.5; arguably, Monkey is accessible to a larger and younger demographic than intended. The 2010 work by Laser, Jenson and Nicotera discuss the how social media and peers have a huge authority on adolescents and the essential benefit for parent engagement. Monkey does not seem to have a platform for parents of young users to moderate their children’s activity on the app, which is concerning due to the natural development that teens go through. Teens seek social acceptance and are more susceptible to peer pressure (Laser et al., 2010), naturally spend less time with parents (Moretti & Peled, 2004) and social networking platforms are popular outlets for the modern world (Curtin, 2017). A 2015 piece by Diane Barth discusses the challenging impact that technology has on the psychological health of youth; on one hand, teens gravitate to social media for the need to be connected and accepted but, on the opposite end, it causes feelings of loneness and anxiety from cyberbullying. Steinberg (2014) also details the need for teens to act in the here-and-now, without much self-control, for fear of missing out and living to the fullest; emotions are intensified. This positions adolescents to make, accept and tolerate riskier behaviors. Lastly, Hillman, Hooper and Choo (2014) speak of the dangers of child exploitation by predators who use social media to connect with vulnerable children, especially those without adequate parent supervision. In essence, Monkey was designed to help connect teens with other teens for a positive and supportive environment but it does not function as it was intended. There are users who display an alarming amount of content that is neither positive nor supportive, others lie in their profile and children as young as 10 or 11 can access Monkey and talk to peers in their late teens, mid-twenties or older. The app tries to protect users from harm but these actions seem to be more reactive than proactive. For Monkey to truly work as intended it needs a huge upgrade. Some suggestions include creating outlets for parents to moderate their children’s activity with the app or have parent approval to download the app; increase the age limit or modify the program to keep users in cohorts based on their age; or create a better age verification process. As it stands, this app is most appropriate for individuals over the age of 17 and under the age of 23.

title: Yubo does connect teens, but lacks in safeguarding
body:
As a social worker and advocate for healthy adolescent development, I have been researching apps that appeal to this population.  While Yubo does provide a platform for connection and has developed user guides and a robust private policy, this app lacks in safeguarding adolescents from inappropriate content.
I love the idea of connecting teens locally and globally to learn about different cultures, languages and ideas, but found the content to be often inappropriate; appealing to more of a “hookup culture” or dating site.

title: A few problems
body:
i would totally be giving this app 5 stars, i love it,it has helped me make new friends from all over the place, however i’m only giving it 3 because there is a few issues...
Issue number one, you have to pay to see who swiped you, and if you’re like me, a teen without a job and that has no money, you can’t pay the ridiculous 5.99$ PER WEEK, 9.99$ PER MONTH, or 6.16$ PER 3 MONTHS. It’s the same with all the other little “power packs”, you have to pay to truly enjoy the full version of this app which i believe is crazy. This app is marketed towards TEENS, and more than half of the teens that are on this app are 14 and 15, in other words, not old enough to get a job, and are definitely not about to ask their parents to shovel out money that they work for on some app.
Issue number two, the lives are extremely glitchy/spotty. On this app teens are allowed to go live, just as they would on instagram or tiktok, however the lives that are taken place on this app are buggy to say so the least. The screen of some of the broadcasters will become pixelated, lag.Voices will sound robotic, cut out in the middle of a sentence, or echo/sound like they are in a tunnel. 
Issue number three, the catfishes, now i know with any dating or making friends app there are bound to be some catfishes, HOWEVER, on this app even if you report an obvious catfish, the profile will not get taken down. Not only do catfishes not get taken down, but the obvious adults (which aren’t allowed), the people that only post drugs on their profile, or the people that post nudity/ask for nudes do not get banned/taken down. 
I truly do love this app, but i really wish that these problems were fixed, and fixed soon. If not i’m most likely going to find an app that is similar to this one, but functions better and is more teen/user friendly.

title: Very Frustrating
body:
This app is all around disappointing. I have made many new friends in here but this app makes that more difficult than it needs to be. I have quite a bit of issues with this app that I will discuss below.

Firstly, I’ve been trying to change my swipe age range for weeks now to no avail. Every time I change it, it changes back on its own.

Also, the friends I actually care about on this app are not able to see when I am live and I am not able to see when they are alive. We’ve tried everything from redownloading the app, to restarting our phones and even unfriending to refriend each other. Nothing worked so we’ve decided to take our business elsewhere.

In addition, the search tab is a joke. I have extreme difficulty finding my friends’ lives through the search tab. 

Moreover, the racism on this app is concerning. I believe in freedom of speech but it seems like most of the Caucasian people on this app love to use the n-word regularly and make very racist comments.

Additionally, if your do not want to be harassed for nude pictures constantly this is not the app for you.

Not to mention, the lives are very laggy and quite frustrating. They sometimes require you to restart the app just to fix the connection.

Another problem I face is the rate at which my battery level depleted while using this app. Trust me you might want to keep your device plugged in.

Finally, my account has been blocked for an entire day despite me trying to change my profile to Yubo’s standards. I’ve gotten three messages from the Yubo team so far regarding an issue they had with my face not being completely visible in any of my pictures. This claim was completely false. I have multiple pictures on my profile when my face is completely visible other than my prescribed glasses. I’ve tried in vain to contact Yubo support. This issue is very frustrating for me.

In conclusion, this app really isn’t worth it in my opinion. While I have made friends on here, there are many other ways to make friends online that do not include all the hassle of this app.

title: Great if you need more spam in your life!
body:
The app is an absolute joke. You will receive about 15-20 spam messages per day. There are constant fake accounts popping up, making it nearly impossible to find anyone who’s actually real. There are filters to only show you people in your region, but even the smallest region (“here”) will show you people from other countries, and not just neighboring countries. I’m on the west coast of the US and it commonly shows users from Australia when filtering by “here” or “state” along with every other setting. There are many women openly advertising their “services” with prices, so if you’re looking for a prostitute for the evening, you may find this app useful. Also, there is an incredibly high number of trans users. That’s not my thing, but if it’s yours, may also be worth checking out. If it’s not your thing, you will have your searches filled with trans women/men because there isn’t an option to set your gender to trans. 

Aside from that, if you’re a hacker, the app is great fun to explore. There are serious security holes all over. I spent years contacting them before they fixed some of them (I never got a response from any messages). The two major security issues were; all pictures sent to other users in private messages were accessible by all users. Even when I provided a simple script which demonstrated automated downloading of all images in real time, as well as previously sent pictures, it went ignored for years. The second, and more major issue allowed you to see users exact location. Not as in what city they are in, but more detailed, like which room of their house they are in. I highly suggest not giving the app access to your location, unless you’re in a public area, then disable the location services prior to opening the app when you’re at home. Again, this issue also went ignored for years after reporting it.

title: Was good until the new update. Now it’s a cash grab wig a toxic environment
body: At first before the new update I enjoyed the app. I was constantly meeting new people and getting swiped on. However in the new update there’s an option to “increase your visibility” by paying to become a member. After the new update released I was rarely getting matches. Now either this is a coincidence or they made it so that in order to be viewed by anyone you have to pay basically $9 a month (and must I remind you this is an app targeted for teenagers who probably only have their parents credit card on their phone) to have anybody swipe right on you. So now instead of it being the marketed “optional enhancement” it’s basically now a necessity in order to have any actual success on this app. It also doesn’t help that the update was completely mandatory. So now that you can’t swipe to make friends you have to enter lives, and when I tell you that the lives have some of the most toxic environments that I’ve ever been on, I mean it. While it’s not the developers fault, teenagers will be jerks. The lives have 3 categories of awfulness. 1. Overly exploiting teenage sexuality. Many people feel that the only way to gain attention is through sexualizing themselves. While a lot of the times it’s for clickbait there have genuinely been times where nudity has been featured. 2. Rating. Due to the demographic of this app being teenagers, and your success on this app being based off of how you look, practically everyone on this app is extremely insecure. And how do teenagers (especially immature ones) deal with their insecurities? Well they tell other people that they’re ugly that’s what. I was literally just on a live where with no prompting to the guy in here just said “even though you don’t want me to, I’m gonna rate you. You’re a one”. This was with no prompting because the environment on this app forces people to be quick to want to bring others up just because that’s what makes them feel better about themselves. I’ve built myself up to a point where I’m happy with who I am and know that I’m not ugly, however many people aren’t. I’ve seen perfectly attractive people being insulted with no provocation. And 3. People who just do horrible stuff to get attention. Due to this app being compromised of teenagers many feel that the only way to get views is to be “edgy”. This leads to all the most popular lives consisting of drug use, alcoholism, or my favorite: hate speech. That’s right whenever there’s a live that says “being gay is wrong” or “whites only” or saying the N word but misspelling it, or saying “no gays”, it is guaranteed to be popular. Even if it’s for clickbait there are times that I’ve logged in to find people legitimately advocating for homophobic ideals, or seeing a white person use the N word. And with the average teenager’s psychology, you can bet that this reaffirms their belief that these behaviors are okay. Also sometimes #1 and #3 are combined with such gems as “white girls 🤤” or “White girls only”. And all this would be less of a problem if the swiping system wasn’t so messed up and I could chose who I want to talk to. But since the only places where I can add new friends is through lives it’s pretty difficult. Now don’t get me wrong, there are some nice people who create lives that spread positivity, and I’ve genuinely had some good conversations on this app. However those times are way outshined by the abundance of toxicity in this app’s community.

title: Needs fixes
body:
Not bad but has serious bugs.  Spammers can send chat requests that can't be accepted or rejected and lock it up.  Search needs a lot more options.  Currently it has by a slider distance and what they are looking for (msm, wsm, etc) and age and that's it.

Pics often show on the wrong profile and pics also show incorrectly (as in it shows pic 7 of 5...so yeah it repeats).  Chats get confused and a line you entered will show on all chats even though it's only sent to one person.  

App is also a SERIOUS resource hog.  You really need to close the app completely or it will drain your battery in about 30 minutes.

Profiles have your basic issues with all chat apps.  Fakes, spammers, people selling, druggies galore.
